body_markdown:
Canterbury Park has submitted a request to the[Minnesota Racing Commission](https://mn.gov/mrc/) for a 51-day thoroughbred and quarter horse season that would run from Saturday, May 22 through Saturday, Sept. 25. The[2027 calendar](https://www.canterburypark.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/11/Proposed-2027-Race-Dates-CBY.pdf) offers the same number of race days as 2026 however the meet has been extended by one week to better accommodate the schedules of the trainers expected to participate.[Minnesota statute 240.30](https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/240.30) requires the state’s racetracks to conduct a minimum of 50 days of live racing annually to operate a card club.[Canterbury’s Card Casino](https://www.canterburypark.com/table-games/) revenue is the major funding source of racing purses.


Racing would be conducted primarily on Thursdays and Saturdays at 5 p.m. central and Sundays at 1 p.m. Additional race dates include Fridays, July 23, Aug. 6 and Sept. 24 and Memorial Day, Monday, May 31 and Labor Day, Monday, Sept. 6. A 10-day break is also proposed from July 12 to 21.


“Our summer racing schedule works well for the trainers and owners that have supported Canterbury Park and we expect to welcome them back again in 2027,” company CEO Randy Sampson


Randy Sampson


said. “This schedule combined with efficient and modern facilities in which to train and live, safe racing surfaces, a fun atmosphere and our horsemen-friendly culture will also be attractive to new stables seeking a place to race.”


The 2027 stakes schedule will be released in early January with the first condition book available in February.


“A priority this winter is making potential new trainers and owners aware of the many racing opportunities that we offer for horses of all class levels on both turf and dirt,” Sampson said.


Canterbury Park has the only turf course in the upper Midwest. Last season 48 percent of all thoroughbred races were carded for the turf course. Purses are expected to remain consistent with the 2026 season.


Stall applications will be due in mid-April. Canterbury’s stable area, with 1,070 stalls, a training track, exercise wheel, RV park and multiple dormitories will open for equine arrivals in early May.


The Minnesota Racing Commission will consider Canterbury Park’s request at its December 17 meeting. The commission, an eight-member panel, is appointed by the state’s governor and tasked with overseeing the integrity and safety of horse racing at Minnesota’s two pari-mutuel racetracks.


[See 2027 proposed calendar.](https://www.canterburypark.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/11/Proposed-2027-Race-Dates-CBY.pdf)


Canterbury Park’s 24/7 casino and[simulcast racebook](https://www.canterburypark.com/racebook/) remain open daily.
